chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hammad, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the marriage of Umm Kulthum.
He said: 'Indeed, that was a private part (of the body) that was usurped from us.'

key_terms.غُصِبْنَاهُ: We were usurped / It was taken by force

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'usurped' imply about the marriage of Umm Kulthum in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) characterizes the marriage of Umm Kulthum to the Umayyads as 'usurped' (ghusibnah), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that it was a political imposition rather than a voluntary union. This highlights the concept of *ghasb* (usurpation) applied to the Ahl al-Bayt's marital status, emphasizing their elevated spiritual standing and the temporary nature of their subjugation to caliphal authority. The phrase underscores the distinction between the intrinsic nobility of the Imams' lineage and the external political realities of their time.
